title: bug: PowerShell launcher treats brackets in a project path as a wildcard and refuses an existing checkout
description: Native Windows PowerShell 5.1 real-wrapper fixture with an existing absolute project directory named "control é [x] $;'" exits before CLI launch with 'Project path not found'. Same fixture without [x] launches normally; project discovery uses wildcard-sensitive path tests. Reproduced while testing the accidental Git-write guard; fix literal project-path discovery separately.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (static guard + CI). Create scripts/tests/literal-project-path.test.mjs (node:test, ESM). Header comment: PowerShell reads [ ] (and backtick) in a -Path argument as wildcard syntax, so a project dir named "control é [x] $;'" fails Resolve-Path -Path / Test-Path; PS 5.1 Start-Process also resolves the inherited current location as a wildcard.

Read scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-team.ps1 via new URL('../<name>', import.meta.url); strip the BOM; CRLF->LF.

Scanner rules:
- Skip full-line `#` comments and `<# ... #>` blocks.
- A cmdlet counts only at command position: preceded, after optional whitespace, by line start, `(`, `{`, `|`, `;`, `=` or the keyword `return`.
- Its segment ends at the first `|`, `;` or newline at depth 0, or at the `)`/`}` that closes an enclosing group.
- Text nested in (...) or {...} inside the segment is NOT top level.

Rules:
- G1: these cmdlets need `-LiteralPath` at the top level of their segment: Test-Path, Get-Content, Set-Content, Add-Content, Clear-Content, Out-File, Get-Item, Get-ChildItem, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Remove-Item, Rename-Item, Resolve-Path, Convert-Path, Push-Location, Set-Location, Get-Acl, Set-Acl, Get-FileHash.
  - Exempt an operand on the Env: drive (`Remove-Item Env:X`, `Remove-Item -Path "Env:\$k"`).
  - New-Item is not listed: its -Path is literal by design and it has no -LiteralPath (probed).
- G2: every Start-Process segment contains `-WorkingDirectory` and `WildcardPattern]::Escape(`.

Tests:
(1) Per file: assert.deepEqual(violations, []). Each violation is `<file>:<line>: <trimmed text>`; the message names the rule and the reason. Also assert each file has at least one G1 invocation, so a broken read cannot pass vacuously.
(2) Scanner self-test on an inline sample, asserting the EXACT flagged set:
- `if (-not (Test-Path $a)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $a | Out-Null }` -> Test-Path only
- `$c = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $p | ConvertFrom-Json` -> none
- `Get-ChildItem -Path $d -File -Filter '*.md' | ForEach-Object { Copy-Item -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Destination $t }` -> Get-ChildItem only
- `Test-Path (Get-Item -LiteralPath $p).FullName` -> Test-Path only (a nested literal does not count)
- `# Test-Path $x` -> none
- `Write-Host "run Test-Path by hand"` -> none
- `Remove-Item Env:MOE_X -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` -> none
- `return Get-Content -Path $f` -> Get-Content
- `Start-Process -FilePath node -ArgumentList @($a)` -> G2
- `Start-Process node -WorkingDirectory ([System.Management.Automation.WildcardPattern]::Escape($d))` -> none
Register no tests when argv[2] is `cli` or `start` (the step-2 fake modes).

CI: in .github/workflows/ci.yml, job build-all-platforms, add a NEW step right after "Test agent runtime discovery", with no OS condition:
  - name: Test launcher literal project paths
    run: node --test scripts/tests/literal-project-path.test.mjs
Do not edit the existing node --test lines: task-4e412148 plans to append to one of them.

(b) Convert every remaining G1 site to -LiteralPath and keep every other parameter. The sites below are as of 2026-10-30. Line numbers WILL have moved: 26 upstream ps1-lane tasks land first. So apply the rule to whatever the step-1 guard lists, including their new code.

Forms:
- `Get-Content -Raw -Path $x` -> `Get-Content -LiteralPath $x -Raw`.
- `Set-Content -Path $f -Encoding UTF8 [-NoNewline]` -> `Set-Content -LiteralPath $f -Encoding UTF8 [-NoNewline]`. On both engines, -Path with -Encoding fails for a new bracketed file with "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'Encoding'" (probed).
- `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $d -File -Filter '*.md'`.
- `Copy-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination $dest -Force`. A bracketed -Destination works (probed).

(c) The daemon-start Start-Process gains `-WorkingDirectory ([System.Management.Automation.WildcardPattern]::Escape((Get-Location -PSProvider FileSystem).ProviderPath))`. It is the same directory as before, only escaped. Add a one-line comment: PS 5.1 resolves the inherited current location as a wildcard. Probed facts:
- From a [x] cwd, 5.1 fails with "Cannot perform operation because the wildcard path ... did not resolve to a file"; 7.6 is fine.
- A raw bracketed -WorkingDirectory fails on both engines; an escaped one works on both.

Error handling: keep every existing -ErrorAction (SilentlyContinue / Stop), try/catch and fallback exactly as it is. A genuinely missing path must still take the same branch as today: 'Project path not found', 'not initialized for Moe', the plugin docs/roles fallback, the Serena 'override not found' warning, the dotted codex fallback, and 'Daemon failed to start'. -LiteralPath changes only how the path string is interpreted, never what happens when it is absent.

Leave alone: Env: drive operations, New-Item -Path, Join-Path/Split-Path (string ops), [IO.File] calls, native git -C/argv, and moe-agent.sh. Make no other behavior change. Done when the step-1 guard reports no moe-agent.ps1 violations.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Probe results, PS 5.1.26100 and 7.6.9, on a dir named "control é [x] $;'":
- Resolve-Path/Test-Path with -Path return false/null; with -LiteralPath they work.
- New-Item -Path is literal by design.
- Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath -Filter works. Copy-Item -LiteralPath works with a bracketed -Destination. Set-Content -LiteralPath works.
- Set-Content -Path ... -Encoding UTF8 on a NEW bracketed file throws "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'Encoding'" on both engines.
